Egress is closed by default; policies, by tag, name what a workspace may reach

name: What a workspace reached, what it looked up and what it was refused
Each request to a brokered name as the proxy read it, served or refused and why; and whether each injection's secret is the team's to give
The egress proxy is a process of its own, holding no key of the host's, started again by the runner when it ends
A brokered rule names whose it is, the agent's or the person's: one policy says what each may reach and with what
A WebSocket to a brokered name: its handshake under the rule's headers and scope, then bytes each way
note: The rule's header on the handshake is not read at the origin: the lane's WebSocket echo answers frames, not headers.

note: gRPC's trailers are egressproxy's h2 test against an origin of its own; the lane has no gRPC origin to reach.

note: The lane has no provider credential, so no test has a model answer through the brokered egress: the server is reached, as the agent's user, and nothing is asked of it. The browser's test drives the page with a virtual authenticator, which no real passkey's maker vouches for.

name: Claude Code and Codex signed in from the agent's page: each CLI's own login, run by the supervisor as the agent's user, its credentials kept in the agent's home and never passing through the page
note: The lane has no provider account: it begins a login and sees the provider's page, and finishing one is the unit tests' on each CLI's own output.

name: A person signs Claude Code and Codex in once: every workspace of theirs, plain or a project's, is handed the same credentials and hands back each refresh and logout, and a workspace that names a guest holds none
note: The lane has no provider account: its login is the file the CLI writes, written as the agent's user. Only a workspace its owner's alone through all it came from holds them: a project opened from its prebuild does, but not a prebuild's build, a copy of another person's snapshot, or one made before the release that keeps the mark.

name: The supervisor runs the agent for its owner while it is used: started, paired and listed over the owner's own session on a socket only root opens, and stopped once nobody has used it for half an hour and no chat is at work
note: That it stops once idle is the sweep's unit test on a clock the test moves: no lane waits half an hour.

name: The agent's chats listed on the workspace - titles, paths and times, never a message - reported by its supervisor
Chat mode: the dashboard flips to the person's own chats across their workspaces, grouped by project, with the agent full height and a new chat that makes its workspace
endToEndGap: The RPC is held to the caller's own chats by its unit test, the mode by the dashboard's; no lane opens chat mode in a browser against an agent that has reported.

name: The agent's home is a volume of its own: the chats and sessions outlive the workspace, kept in the installation's store as every disk is, and a new workspace mounts them at its creation
note: Sealed with the workspace's checkpoints, claimed with the launch beside the disk, and moved with the workspace.

An agent in a workspace drives others with spin, on a key it gets for the workspace's own SPIFFE identity - a child of the key that made the workspace, through its host, whatever the workspace's network
note: No forge in the lane: a workspace reaches no private or host address, and no test repository has a credential in CI yet, so an agent opening a pull request is not run.

A workspace's last hour of CPU, memory and network against what it holds, for its owner

note: A resume whose recorded release was collected since has no test against the stack.

name: AWS only
note: The Terraform module is the one supported install; nothing else is packaged or tested.

name: x86-64 only
note: Runners are x86-64 machines with nested virtualization.

name: The CLI runs on Linux and macOS
note: x86-64 and Arm of each; there is no Windows build.

name: One region, one control plane
note: A machine that fails is replaced in minutes, not seconds.

name: No GPUs
note: A preset names the class of runner its workspaces run on, and no class hands a workspace a GPU.

name: Linux guests only
note: Booted with the kernel spin provides.

name: No IPv6 inside a workspace
TCP only for published ports
A diff does not see everything
note: A file is hashed only when its size, inode or times changed; extended attributes are not compared.

name: A memory snapshot resumes only on the same machine
note: The same QEMU, guest kernel and guest init; a disk restore has no such limit.

name: Disk chains have a limit
note: At the limit the top layer grows instead, so less of the recent work is in the bucket.

name: Work since the last upload can be lost
note: A runner uploads writes in layers, on the RPO, on snapshot and on stop; what it had not uploaded goes with it.

name: No multi-factor authentication of Spinbox's own
note: Sign in through a provider that enforces it.

name: No team invitations
note: A person signs in once before they can be added to a team; a workspace's guests are invited by email.

name: Team roles are fixed
note: Owner, admin and member.

name: Nothing pages the operator
note: Metrics, logs and traces stay inside the installation; alert rules fire in its Grafana and no contact point tells anyone. A workspace's owner is emailed when it waits for them.

name: An update is one way
note: A release older than the one that last started the database refuses to start on it.
